description: Phase-DISCIPLINE — output discipline + tool-result cap + clarification exit ramp. Triggered 2026-05-21 by live observation: Aura received vague 'trova un cliente e stampalo' on a 90-row source, used execute_code to read everything, then DUMPED all 90 rows as a 36-sec wall-of-text reply. Substrate is fine (bench post-Wave-A-fix = 90%); the dump is a BEHAVIOR + boundary problem. 4-repo research (D:\tmp\picobot + codex + cli-printing-press + openhuman) converges on: TOOL-SIDE BYTE CAP at the boundary (4-16 KiB across the 4 repos), behavior prompt rules ('ack first, never restate tool output'), and an ask_user_clarification first-class tool as the exit ramp from vague requests. Research artifacts: docs/restructure-research/{picobot,codex,cli-printing-press,openhuman}-output-discipline-2026-05-21.md. 5 atomic stories. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Audit and remove agent-loop fallback that emits raw tool result as user-facing reply
userStories.description: Picobot's analysis flagged a structural anti-pattern at D:/tmp/picobot/internal/agent/loop.go:283-285 and 350-352: when the LLM returns empty content after a tool call, the loop sets finalContent = lastToolResult — so the next surface (Telegram outbound) ships raw tool bytes to the user. Aura may have the same bug. (a) GREP for the equivalent pattern in internal/agent/loop.go, internal/agent/executor.go, internal/chat/agentloop.go, internal/channels/telegram/invocation_builder.go: any `if finalContent == ''`, `if reply == ''`, `if assistant.Content == ''` followed by a fallback that reads from tool results, last tool, or executions summary. (b) Note: this is DIFFERENT from the deliberate 'final answer = synthesized from prior tool output' that the LLM produces — we're looking for an UNTAGGED echo where the runtime substitutes raw tool bytes because the LLM emitted nothing. (c) If FOUND: replace the substitution with a short canned fallback message ('Ho elaborato i risultati ma non ho una risposta da darti. Vuoi che riassuma cosa ho trovato?') AND a structured agent_note recording the empty-LLM event for later debugging. (d) If NOT FOUND: ship a test that PROVES the loop currently does NOT substitute — supply a stubbed LLM that returns empty Content + a tool that returns 'RAW_TOOL_BYTES_SHOULD_NEVER_BE_USER_VISIBLE', assert the user-facing reply does NOT contain that string. The test acts as a regression gate against re-introducing the anti-pattern later. (e) Document the result in the commit body — 'audit-only: pattern not present, regression test added' OR 'pattern found at file:line — replaced with canned message + agent_note'.
acceptanceCriteria: Grep performed across internal/agent/, internal/chat/, internal/channels/ for fallback patterns that emit tool bytes when LLM returns empty content

userStories.title: Tool-side byte cap — boundOutput wrapper at Execute() return with truncation marker
userStories.description: Universal pattern across all 4 research repos: cap tool stdout/result at the TOOL boundary, not the agent layer. picobot caps web_search to 5 topics; codex truncates to 10 KB; openhuman to 16 KiB; cli-printing-press to 4 KiB. Aura's execute_code currently has no cap → 90-row DataFrame goes into the LLM context unmediated → LLM gets confused and emits the wall-of-text. (a) NEW HELPER internal/agent/tools/registry/boundoutput.go: BoundOutput(content string, maxBytes int, maxRows int) (string, bool) — returns (capped, truncated). If content fits both caps, returns unchanged. Otherwise: clip to maxBytes (UTF-8 safe — don't break mid-rune), then count rows from the start; if rowCount > maxRows, clip again to maxRows rows. Append marker: '\n\n[truncated: showing first {actualBytes} bytes / {actualRows} rows of {totalBytes} / {totalRows}. Re-run with a narrower query OR ask the user what subset they want.]'. (b) DEFAULT CAPS: maxBytes=8192 (middle of the 4-16 KiB convergence — codex 10 KB / openhuman 16 KiB / cli-printing-press 4 KiB), maxRows=20. Tunable per-tool via Tool.OutputCap struct field (zero = use defaults). (c) WIRE AT BOUNDARY: at internal/agent/tools/registry/registry.go Execute return, wrap every successful tool result through BoundOutput before returning to the agent loop. errors from BoundOutput itself are not possible (it always succeeds), so no error path change. (d) PER-TOOL OVERRIDE: tools that legitimately return larger payloads (e.g., file action=read on a 50 KB markdown file the user asked for verbatim) set OutputCap.MaxBytes higher. file action=read default = 16384 (asking for a file body implies the user wants more bytes than for a search). execute_code default uses the global 8192. search_memory default = 8192. doc creation tools (action=xlsx/docx/pdf) bypass the cap entirely (they return a path, not content). (e) TEST: internal/agent/tools/registry/boundoutput_test.go: TestBoundOutput_BelowCaps_NoChange, TestBoundOutput_AboveBytes_ClipsAndMarks, TestBoundOutput_AboveRows_ClipsAndMarks, TestBoundOutput_UTF8Safe (don't split mid-rune on accented Italian chars), TestBoundOutput_MarkerIsLLMReadable (marker contains 'truncated' AND 'narrower' AND 'ask the user'). (f) INVARIANT: existing tools continue to work — no test in internal/agent/ should fail. Document any test that needs to be relaxed because it asserted a long output that now gets capped (rare; flag in commit body).

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read all 4 research docs in docs/restructure-research/. (2) Read internal/agent/tools/registry/registry.go Execute method (and any sibling like dispatcher.go). (3) Read existing Tool / ToolDefinition struct shape in internal/agent/tools/registry/types.go (or similar). (4) Check whether tools currently return raw content strings or wrapped DTOs — affects where BoundOutput plugs in. UTF-8 SAFETY: use utf8.RuneCountInString + range-over-string indexing; never byte-slice into a UTF-8 string at arbitrary offsets. ROW COUNTING: rows = lines (split on '\n'). For JSON-shaped tool output (e.g., search_memory results), each top-level result item is a 'row' even if multi-line — flag this nuance in a comment; for v0 the line-split is acceptable. MARKER FORMAT: must be parsable by both LLM and humans. Example: `[truncated: 8192 of 47391 bytes (17%), 20 of 90 rows. Re-run with a narrower query OR ask the user what subset they want.]`. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: do NOT touch the prompt overlays — that's US-DRIFT-03's job. Do NOT add the ask_user_clarification tool here — that's US-DRIFT-04. Do NOT change tool descriptions — that's US-DRIFT-05. Only the cap. PERF: BoundOutput is O(n) on content; tools typically return <100 KB so negligible. EDGE CASE: empty content (e.g., shell command that produced no output) — return as-is, no marker. WHEN ALREADY TRUNCATED UPSTREAM: if the content already ends with a marker (e.g., source/file already capped earlier in the pipeline), DON'T add a second marker — detect 'truncated' substring near the end and skip.

userStories.title: Response-style block in AGENT.md — synthesize, never restate tool output
userStories.description: openhuman's orchestrator/prompt.md:82-132 is 50 lines of explicit response-style rules: 'text-a-friend, lowercase, one idea per bubble, ack first then result, never restate the tool output' + 4 worked examples. codex has similar verbosity budgets keyed to task size (gpt_5_2_prompt.md:225-230). Aura's current AGENT.md has the WRONG advice on retrieval ('NON cercare in memoria per domande tecniche generiche' was the old bug, recently fixed) but has NOTHING on output style. This story adds a dedicated section that trains Aura to synthesize. (a) NEW SECTION in runtime-workspace/AGENT.md AND internal/config/defaults/AGENT.md (defaults must mirror runtime so fresh clones get the same rule): `## Stile risposta — sintesi obbligatoria`. (b) RULES (mirror openhuman + codex + adapt to Italian Telegram chat): (1) NEVER restate the raw tool output. The tool result is INTERNAL context — the user does not see it. Your reply is YOUR distillation. (2) Lunghezza per dimensione del task: domanda puntuale (chi/quando/dove) = 1-3 frasi MAX. Lista breve = 5-10 elementi MAX. Lista lunga = chiedi 'vuoi tutti o solo i primi N?' PRIMA di stampare. (3) Pattern obbligatorio per dati tabulari: prima riassumi (es. '90 clienti, 4 colonne'), poi mostra al MAX 5 esempi rappresentativi, poi 'vuoi i restanti N? quali colonne / filtri?'. (4) Quando un tool ritorna un marker `[truncated...]`, NON ignorarlo — riformula la domanda all'utente o usa una query più stretta. (5) execute_code è INTERNO. Lo usi per processare + filtrare. La risposta al user NON contiene mai l'stdout grezzo di execute_code. (c) 4 WORKED EXAMPLES (matching the openhuman pattern), all in Italian, all calibrated to Telegram chat: (i) 'Trova un cliente e stampalo' → ask 'quale cliente? nome / codice / criterio?'; (ii) 'Riassumi il documento' → 3-5 bullet (no tool dump); (iii) 'Quali sono i clienti della zona PIE?' → '4 clienti: AGRIMAT (597425), ...' (compact list); (iv) 'Crea un xlsx dei clienti' → doc action=xlsx, then 'Pronto: /workspace/clienti.xlsx — 90 righe, 4 colonne'. (d) ADD to the existing 'Anti-pattern' section at the bottom: 'wall-of-text dump from tool output — VIETATO'. (e) Verify the section flows in BOTH files (alphabetical / section-order consistency between runtime and defaults).

userStories.title: ask_user_clarification tool — first-class exit ramp from vague requests
userStories.description: openhuman's tools/impl/agent/ask_clarification.rs is wired into the orchestrator's Direct-First decision tree as a primary tool. When the user sends a vague prompt ('Trova un cliente' → which? what fields?), instead of best-effort = fetch everything, the agent calls ask_user_clarification with a structured question + 2-4 option chips. The chat surface renders these as inline buttons / quick replies; the user picks one, agent resumes with the disambiguated intent. (a) NEW TOOL internal/agent/tools/registry/ask_user_clarification.go: AskUserClarificationTool. Name = 'ask_user_clarification'. Parameters: {question string required, options []{label string, value string} max 4, free_text_allowed bool default true}. (b) EXECUTE returns a structured AwaitingUserInput payload — the agent loop must PAUSE here (similar to how Aura's existing ErrAwaitingUserInput is handled — grep registry/ for the pattern; AskUserResumeTool may already exist). The pause emits an OutboundEvent to the channel (Telegram = sends the question with option chips as inline buttons OR as a numbered list with reply prompts; web = sends a structured question payload the dashboard renders as buttons). (c) AGENT LOOP INTEGRATION: ensure the existing pause-and-resume infrastructure picks this up. Pattern reference: internal/agent/tools/registry/ has tools that return ErrAwaitingUserInput; reuse that. (d) PROMPT WIRING: AGENT.md (and internal/config/defaults/AGENT.md) gains a bullet in the existing 'Esecuzione e tool' section: 'Quando una richiesta è ambigua (es. \'trova un cliente\' senza criterio), chiama PRIMA ask_user_clarification con 2-3 opzioni concrete invece di best-effort. Costa 1 round trip ma evita un dump da 90 righe.'. (e) TEST internal/agent/tools/registry/ask_user_clarification_test.go: TestAskUserClarification_Parameters (schema correct), TestAskUserClarification_ExecuteReturnsAwaitingUserInput (returns the pause signal), TestAskUserClarification_OptionsCapped (more than 4 options is an error). (f) INTEGRATION TEST internal/agent/loop_test.go: a probe scenario where the agent receives 'find a customer' on a 90-row dataset → asserts ask_user_clarification was called (NOT execute_code) → asserts the loop paused with the question payload. (g) Telegram channel: the question + options should render as one message with a 'numbered list' (1. Per nome | 2. Per codice | 3. Mostrami i primi 5) — keep it simple, don't require inline keyboard wiring (that's a separate Telegram-channel polish).

userStories.title: Tool description audit — operational markers, no user-facing language
userStories.description: codex's core/src/tools/handlers/shell_spec.rs:198 deliberately keeps tool descriptions PURELY OPERATIONAL — no 'show output to user' suggestions. cli-printing-press's mcpdesc.Compose injects behavioral markers ('Destructive.', 'Read-only.', 'List-capped at 20.') so the LLM learns BY DESCRIPTION-SHAPE that 'show some, offer more' is the default. Aura's current tool descriptions are mixed: some say what they DO (good), some hint at user-visibility (e.g., 'returns the response so the user can see X'). This story audits + cleans them. (a) GREP internal/agent/tools/registry/ for Description() / Definition() return strings — list every tool's description. (b) For EACH tool, ensure the description: (i) describes WHAT it does (the action), (ii) lists REQUIRED + OPTIONAL parameters by action when action-dispatched, (iii) flags BEHAVIORAL CONSTRAINTS at the start: 'Destructive.', 'Read-only.', 'Returns capped list (20).', 'Returns paths only.', 'Returns a structured envelope, not raw text.'. (iv) does NOT say 'so the user can see' / 'show the result to the user' / similar — the LLM, not the description, decides what to emit. (c) PRIORITIES for the audit (these are the tools the bench / live conv shows being misused most): execute_code (must say 'Read-only stdout, 8192-byte cap, results are INTERNAL to the agent'), execute_shell (same), source action=read (must say 'Returns the source archive bytes, 16384-byte cap'), file action=read (same), web action=search (must say 'Returns top-5 results'), search_memory (must say 'Returns top-10 hits, INTERNAL — synthesize before replying'). (d) doc action=xlsx|docx|pdf descriptions should emphasize they return a PATH, not content — these are the right tool for 'create a file', not execute_code. (e) GENERATE A REPORT in commit body: each tool's old description vs new description, ≤10 lines per tool, just the deltas. (f) NO code logic changes — only description strings. (g) TEST: existing tests should pass. Add internal/agent/tools/registry/description_audit_test.go that enforces the markers — for every registered tool, the description must start with one of {'Destructive.', 'Read-only.', 'Returns ...'} OR start with the action verb in present tense (Create / Read / Delete). Test fails loudly if a future tool description sneaks in without the discipline.

(2) GREP `internal/agent/tools/registry/ -E 'Description\(\) string'` to find every tool. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: DO NOT change the parameters / schema / Execute() logic of any tool.
